When we write an expression like $\maroonD{4}^\blueE{3}$, we call $\maroonD{4}$ the $\maroonD{\text{base}}$, and we call $\blueE{3}$ the $\blueE{\text{exponent}}$.

The $\blueE{\text{exponent}}$ tells us how many factors of the $\maroonD{\text{base}}$ we should multiply to find the value of the expression.

For example, $\maroonD{5}^\blueE{2} = \maroonD{5} \cdot \maroonD{5}$ and $\maroonD{7}^\blueE{4} = \maroonD{7} \cdot \maroonD{7} \cdot \maroonD{7} \cdot \maroonD{7}$.
